newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French September bond and PIBOR futures closed up, but slightly off their highs after a day of moderate trading driven largely by rises in Bunds and helped by interest from U.S. investors.

Analysts and traders said the market was relatively calm, trading "almost tick for tick" with bunds. Towards the end of the session, the notionnel was lifted as U.S. investors continued their recent buying of European assets.
U.S. interest stems partly from worries about a drop in the U.S. bond market tied to a rebound in the Japanese economy.

The markets were also lifted by government comments about 1998 ministerial budget instruction letters. Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's office said the letters contained no precise deficit target and said the deficit criteria in the Maastricht treaty should be interpreted as a trend.
This fuelled confidence EMU would start on time with a softer euro. Dealers said investors appeared to prefer that scenario to a delay.
Investors feel that Jospin may allow the deficit to be higher than three percent, but that he will keep it close enough to that mark to qualify France for EMU, one analyst said.
"There is a feeling that the deficit is likely to overshoot but that the government will keep France on track for EMU," said one analyst at a U.S. investment bank in Paris.
After the close, Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said the new government's spending measures would not increase France's deficit.
"The siutation is serious, everyone thinks it, both on state spending and on welfare spending," he said.
"In no way, therefore, will there be a worsening of the deficit due to this new spending," he told the French Senate, the upper house of parliament.
The franc was firm at 3.3737 per mark compared to 3.3745 on Wednesday, well within a range it has carved out in recent sessions.
